correctness.rationale: The exact common backward reset age is exponential and makes the stationary logarithms a Gaussian variance-mean mixture with independent innovations conditional on age. Renewal gives the all-n integral, its unique saddle z=1/s_n and Gaussian Mills/Laplace analysis give the exact C_n y^{-(n-1)/2} exp(-k_n y) equivalent. The potentially non-Mills large-age zone for positive drift decays at rate r/a>k_n. Univariate transform inversion independently gives c1 exp(-k1 y). Rate identities establish strict exponent ordering, drift monotonicity and the three iterated n regimes. The 128-assertion checker numerically integrates the original integral at selected parameters and tests coefficients; no finite test supports a universal limit without the proof. Assumptions: n fixed first, sigma,r>0, a real, synchronous resets to 1, independent noises. No simultaneous n/y limit.

value.rationale: Collective exceedances are natural in systems with synchronized financial crashes or simultaneous renewal of independently fluctuating multiplicative populations. Single-particle stationary Pareto laws cannot determine their n-fold rare-event probability. The theorem supplies the full sharp prefactor and exact quantile-standardized exponent. Its drift-sign trichotomy (bounded, sqrt(n), linear) classifies a structural competition between shared rare ages and independent Brownian innovations. Independent and shared reset clocks have identical one-point laws but asymptotically different n-fold rare risks, at all finite n>=2, a practically interpretable distinction. This is not a fixed parameter substitution, textbook normalization or unmotivated small slice. Limits: iterated threshold then n, no correlated Brownian noise or partial-batch resetting.
